title: Random ID Generator
description: Generate URL-safe random IDs in the browser with a chosen length and alphabet. Uses crypto.getRandomValues, not Math.random, and nothing is stored.
intro: Create short IDs for filenames, test data or local prototypes. Pick the length and whether to include symbols that stay safe in URLs.
blurb: Create URL-safe random IDs locally with the Web Crypto random source.
howItWorks: Length is limited to 4–64 characters and the batch size to 50 IDs.
Each character is chosen with crypto.getRandomValues so the source is the browser CSPRNG.
The URL-safe alphabet avoids characters that need encoding in paths.
examples: Length 21 with the URL-safe alphabet matches the usual NanoID size.
Hex mode returns only 0-9 and a-f, useful for short tokens.
A count of 5 prints five IDs, one per line.

faq.a: No. They are random strings, not RFC 4122 UUIDs. Use the UUID generator when you need that format.
The randomness is strong, but this page is for identifiers. Use the password generator for passwords with explicit character rules.
